videos.clip.V0Y3e9A2X0s.title: Every Abrasive Belt Joint Is Carefully Glued by Hand — Quality You Can Rely On
videos.clip.V0Y3e9A2X0s.body: The lap joint is the weakest point of a sanding belt: a poorly bonded seam splits mid-run and drags on the workpiece. This clip shows the joint being glued and cured by hand, one belt at a time, before the strip is cut and shipped. For distributors ordering long-running belts, the bond is the spec that decides whether a belt finishes the job or fails early.

videos.clip.xMMe9Dz0Enk.title: How We Slit Abrasive Cloth Rolls to Your Exact Width — Factory Process
videos.clip.xMMe9Dz0Enk.body: Master rolls of abrasive cloth are wider than any finished belt. This clip follows one master roll being slit to a named width: the cloth is measured on the guide, fed through the slitter, and checked against the ruler before it is wound into a strip. The point for buyers is that width is cut to your specification, not trimmed off a fixed list, so the size you confirm is the size that ships.
videos.clip.xMMe9Dz0Enk.b1: From master roll to finished width
videos.clip.xMMe9Dz0Enk.b2: Slitting to your exact belt size
videos.clip.pTNrvW_n84k.title: Send Us Your Size + Grit + Quantity — Get Custom Abrasive Belts Fast
videos.clip.pTNrvW_n84k.body: Custom abrasive belts come down to three numbers: the width, the grit, and the quantity. This clip lays out the range we convert, every size and width, grits from coarse to fine, red aluminium oxide, blue zirconia and green silicon carbide, with multi-layer builds where the application needs them. Send the three numbers and we quote against a belt matched to them, not a closest match.
videos.clip.pTNrvW_n84k.b1: Three numbers define a custom belt
videos.clip.pTNrvW_n84k.b3: Red, blue and green abrasive builds
videos.clip.QXIjANwAcg8.title: White Sanding Discs for Paint & Clear Coat — Fine Finish Every Time
videos.clip.QXIjANwAcg8.body: White hook-and-loop sanding discs are the fine-stage discs for paint and clear coat: they cut evenly without throwing deep scratch marks. This clip shows them stuck to a sander pad working down a painted surface, no slipping, no swirl, and a finish ready for the next coat. The discs come in 4-inch and larger sizes; grit is chosen to the stage of the paint work.

videos.clip.GUjrAfcpj0Q.title: Flap Disc Factory Direct — Automated Manufacturing & Bulk Stock Ready
videos.clip.GUjrAfcpj0Q.body: MoTai runs the flap disc line on automated equipment, from abrasive cloth flaps to finished, packed discs ready to ship, all in-house. This clip moves down the line as flaps are wound onto backing, the disc is trimmed and the adhesive is cured under heat, then the finished flap discs are counted and packed. For bulk buyers, the automation is the answer to the question of whether a supplier can hold grit and build consistent across a large order.
videos.clip.GUjrAfcpj0Q.b1: Flap discs on an automated line
videos.clip.GUjrAfcpj0Q.b3: Consistent grit across a bulk run
videos.clip.5Fz6chdSZMo.title: Flexible Sanding Sponge Blocks — High Elasticity, Fast Rebound for Curved Surfaces
videos.clip.5Fz6chdSZMo.body: Sanding sponge blocks are built from high-elasticity foam: tough, flexible and quick to rebound, so they conform to curves and keep their shape through repeated use. This clip presses a block against a curved surface to show how it follows the contour and bounces back. The pads and blocks are supplied in multi-grit, double-sided and die-cut formats, and can be reused after cleaning.
videos.clip.dtX-jOHM21g.title: Custom Sanding Belts — Made to Your Grit & Size | Motai Materials Factory
videos.clip.dtX-jOHM21g.body: MoTai Materials is a professional abrasive belt manufacturer. This clip walks through the workshop: wide abrasive cloth rolls are slit to a named width, the grain and backing are checked, the strip is finished and wound, and the belts are packed ready for shipment. The belts are made to your grit and size, with red aluminium oxide, blue zirconia and green silicon carbide builds available.
